title: Infecting human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells with SARS-CoV-2
protocol: Calculate the required volume of virus stock for an MOI of 0.01 PFU per cell.
Prepare one additional flask per experiment for the mock control.
Remove the supernatant from the flasks.
Add the diluted inoculum to all flasks to be inoculated.
Add 3 mL of D3 medium to the mock control flask.
Incubate for 30 minutes inside the microbiological safety cabinet to allow the virus to attach.
Redistribute the supernatant repeatedly to prevent cells from drying out.
Remove and dispose of the supernatant as infectious waste according to local regulations.
Rinse all flasks twice with 10 mL D2.
Add 15 mL of D2 to each flask.
Incubate at 37°C in a 5% CO2 environment.
Observe cell monolayers for signs of cytopathic effect (CPE) starting from 2 days post infection, twice daily (morning and afternoon).
Harvest the supernatant into a centrifuge tube once fulminant CPE is observed.
Dispose of the flasks and remaining cells in accordance with local safety regulations.
Transfer the supernatant of the mock control flask into another centrifuge tube.
Pellet the cell debris by centrifugation at 500 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer 200–1000 μL aliquots of the supernatant into screw cap tubes.
Transfer a 500 μL aliquot of the mock control supernatant into a screw cap tube.
Store the aliquots at −80°C.
Plate 5×10^5 Vero E6 cells in 2 mL complete growth medium per well of a six-well plate.
Incubate overnight (16 h) at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Alternatively, plate 1.5×10^5 Vero E6 cells in 2 mL growth medium per well of a six-well plate.
Incubate for 3 days at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Confirm that the cells have formed a confluent monolayer by observing them under the microscope.
Take 900 μL D2 and add to each tube/well.
Transfer 100 μL virus to the first tube/well.
Mix the first virus dilution by pipetting up and down several times.
Transfer 100 μL of this diluted virus into the second tube/well.
Continue tenfold dilution series to 10^-6 dilution.
Repeat step for every virus stock and for the mock control supernatant.
Aspirate the medium from each well of one 6-well plate.
Transfer 0.5 mL of each virus dilution into a well, starting with the highest dilution (10−6) and working up to the lowest dilution.
Incubate at room temperature for 40 minutes, gently tilting the plates every 5 minutes.
Add 2 mL overlay medium to each well without removing the supernatant.
Mix overlay and inoculum by gently swirling the plate.
Incubate undisturbed at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration and dispose as contaminated waste.
Add 5 mL fixative per well and incubate for a minimum of 1 hour at room temperature inside the microbiological safety cabinet.
Remove the fixative and add 2 mL PBS per well.
Remove the PBS and add a minimum of 1 mL staining solution to each well.
Incubate for approximately 4 hours or until sufficient staining is observed.
Remove the staining solution.
Gently wash away the remaining staining solution with water, taking care not to damage the cell monolayer.
Invert the plates and allow the cell monolayer to air dry.
Turn on the hood and spray down with 70% ethanol.
Estimate the total volume of fresh blood or bone marrow (BM) aspirate that you have.
Dilute the blood or BM 2:1 with PBS.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 20°C.
Mix blood or bone marrow with an appropriate volume of PBS.
Prepare 15 mL of Ficoll into 50 mL falcon tubes.
Layer 30 mL of mixed blood gently over the prepared Ficcoll without mixing them.
Spin down at 450 g for 30 minutes and at 20°C–25°C without brake.
Collect the thin layer of mononuclear cells between serum and Ficoll after centrifugation.
Pipette 30 mL of blood very gently and angle the tube horizontally to avoid mixing it with the Ficoll.
Centrifuge the sample.
Take the mononuclear cell layer using a pipette.
Transfer the mononuclear cell layer to a new 50 mL falcon tube.
Pool mononuclear cell layers from several falcons until you have 20-25 mL in total.
Dilute the pooled cells 1:1 with PBS+2% FBS.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 20°C.
Remove the supernatant from all of the falcon tubes.
Resuspend one cell pellet with 20 mL ammonium chloride.
Transfer this resuspended cell pellet to the next falcon and use it to resuspend the next pellet.
Repeat the process to resuspend up to 5 cell pellets in 20 mL ammonium chloride.
Leave the solution at 20°C–25°C for 5 min.
Add 2 mL of pure FBS (heat-inactivated) to buffer the lysis.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 20°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL 2% FBS/PBS.
Count the cells.
Continue with the HSPC purification.
Pause point: Freeze the cells in FBS with 10% DMSO.
Use the EasySep Human Progenitor Cell Enrichment kit.
Prepare a mononuclear cell suspension at 5 × 10^7 cells per mL in 5 mL polystyrene tubes, up to a maximum volume of 2 mL.
Add 50 μL/mL of Enrichment Cocktail and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 15 minutes.
Add 100 μL of Magnetic particles per mL of sample and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Top up to 2.5 mL with 2% FBS/PBS and place the tube into a magnet; incubate at 20°C–25°C for 10 minutes.
Discard the magnetic beads attached to lineage cells.
Transfer the non-magnetic cell suspension carefully with a pipette into a new 5 mL polystyrene tube.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes at 20°C.
Stain the enriched cell suspension with the antibody cocktail listed in the key resources table.
Define and sort for hematopoietic stem cells and erythroid progenitors.
Prepare the flow buffer by mixing 2% FBS in PBS.
Multiply the volumes of each reagent by N+1, where N is the number of samples.
Mix all reagents thoroughly via pipetting to create a master mix for antibody cocktail staining.
Stain each sample in the prepared solution containing flow buffer and antibodies.
Ensure optimal titers of staining volumes prior to experiment execution based on cell number and marker expression levels.
Multiply reagent volumes according to total volume used per sample if determined necessary.
Handle antibody vials without direct exposure to light to avoid photobleaching.
Centrifuge the polystyrene tubes with the non-magnetic cell suspension for 5 min at 300 g and 20°C.
Remove the supernatant from the sample tubes.
Add the necessary volume of antibody cocktail per sample to the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet of cells in each tube in the antibody cocktail via pipetting.
Incubate the samples at 4°C for 30–60 min, covering with aluminum foil if necessary to protect from light.
After the incubation period finishes, wash the samples by adding flow buffer at a volume which is at least 10-fold the staining volume.
Centrifuge the samples for 5 min at 300 g and 20°C.
Prepare a solution of DAPI diluted 1:1000 in the flow buffer.
Remove the supernatant from the sample tubes.
Resuspend the pellets in the DAPI solution via pipetting.
Filter the samples to remove any clumps in the cell suspension that may block the sorter.
Prepare 4 × 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes for FACS collection.
Add 200 μL of pure FBS into each tube.
Centrifuge sorted cell populations at 300 g for 5 min at 20°C.
Resuspend cells in StemSpan SFEM supplemented with rhFLT-3L, rhSCF, and rhTPO.
Infect Hematopoietic cells with SARS-CoV-2 at a MOI of 0.5 or 5 PFU per cell.
Incubate infected cells for 30 minutes to analyze binding capacity.
Incubate infected cells for 24 hours to analyze active viral infection.
Transfer cells from the 48-well plate to 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Wash cells three times with PBS (4 minutes at 300 g).
Lose unbound virus by washing.
Lysis the pellet with RLT buffer and vortex thoroughly.
Store samples in RLT buffer at −15°C to −25°C for up to 3–4 weeks.
Perform RNA isolation according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute using 13 μl elution buffer to yield 11 μl of RNA.
Use all 11 μL of RNA for cDNA synthesis with SuperScript III First-Strand Synthesis system.
Incubate the different hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells during the 24 h infection period in 48 well-plates, using 400 μL media (same conditions as in step 58).
After 24 h of infection, add 1 ml of methylcellulose to the media using blunt end needles.
Thoroughly mix the cells in the media with the methylcellulose using a 2 mL syringe.
Divide the methylcellulose mixture into two wells of 12 well-plates, adding 700 μL to each well.
Add 2 mL PBS into three empty wells of the 12-well plate to prevent drying out during incubation.
Incubate for 10–14 days in the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Start screening colony plates under the microscope by day 7 to ensure individual colonies can be picked.
Check the colonies under the microscope to count, score, and pick them.
Choose the appropriate slide holder for individual plates or multi-well plates based on the microscope.
Mark the plate with a pen at the bottom (6 o'clock position).
Start counting from the top left of the plate and work across.
When reaching the other side, go down and work across from right to left.
Repeat this process to cover the entire area of the plate.
Prepare 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes with 350 μL of RLT buffer for each colony.
Pick and score each colony using a p10 pipette set at 10 μL.
Transfer the colony/methylcellulose mixture into the RLT buffer by pipetting up and down repeatedly.
Press all the way down to fully dispense from the pipette tip.
Discard the pipette tip and change to a new one.
Work your way around the plate, repeating the process until completion.
Check the borders starting in the top left corner again.
Rotate the plate while focusing on the same part of the plate throughout.
Mark the plate to know when you have fully rotated it.
Proceed to RNA extraction for viral quantification from different colonies.
Perform retrotranscription as part of the viral quantification procedure.
Conduct RT-qPCR for viral quantification.
